distinct-operations-need-tools-01.graded_text: Agents can search page content across the workspace in one call, through a dedicated search tool or a content query on a listing tool, with explicit scope and pagination, instead of reading pages one by one. The query uses familiar text-search semantics (plain text, phrase, or regular expression) rather than a bespoke query language.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:6 adds a dedicated tool: "| `search_pages` | `{ query, folder?, cursor?, limit? }` | Searches page titles and Markdown content across the workspace, or within `folder` and its subfolders. Returns `{ results: [{ path, title, snippet }], next_cursor? }`, best match first. Default 20 per page." That gives explicit scope (whole workspace or `folder` and its subfolders) and pagination (cursor/limit/next_cursor). Query semantics are ordinary text search, at A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:15: "`query` matches case-insensitively. Every word must appear in the page, and a `\"quoted phrase\"` must appear exactly." That is plain text plus phrase, not a bespoke query language.

distinct-operations-need-tools-02.graded_text: Placing a print order is its own tool, not a file write, a special path, or a flag on an existing tool, because it charges money and ships goods.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:11 adds a separate tool: "| `order_prints` | `{ idempotency_key, paths[], copies, ship_to }` | Orders `copies` printed, bound copies of the listed pages ... charges the workspace's card on file, and ships them to `ship_to`. Requires the Editor role." It is not a flag on write_page or a special path. The rows for write_page, edit_page and delete_pages (lines 8-10) are byte-identical to fixture/docs/mcp-tools.md.

distinct-operations-need-tools-03.graded_text: A retried print-order call after a timeout cannot charge twice: the design states an idempotency key, a single-use quote or order ID, or an equivalent server-side guard.

votes.e: A/project/docs/mcp-tools.md:22: "`idempotency_key` is required. ... resend the same one when retrying a call that timed out or returned no answer. A repeat call with a key the workspace has already used returns the original order with `replayed: true` and charges nothing. Reusing a key with different `paths`, `copies`, or `ship_to` is refused." Line 27 also covers an in-flight retry: "To get the outcome of a `processing` order, call again with the same `idempotency_key`."

distinct-operations-need-tools-04.graded_text: The catalog adds no generic execute, run, or action tool.
